verdicts.misleading_risk: Moderate. (1) Writing title and authors into data/site.yaml duplicates the template README, so the two can drift. (2) Naming 'version 0.0.2' would go stale, because it matches neither a tag nor template_version 0.1.15. (3) A bare '#cite' footer href breaks on every page except the home page. (4) The phrase 'recommended paper' is not in the README. The README only lists the preprint under 'Citation: please cite the project'. Use the README's own wording.
verdicts.refined_proposal:
Build it, but smaller and with the drift risk closed. Severity is major, not blocker.
1. DESIGN.md first: add a 'Citation block' pattern.
2. Replace the dead `links.citation_doi` in data/site.yaml (nothing in scripts reads it) with a `citation:` block holding the preprint title, its five authors as printed on arXiv, and DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2603.10704. Add the Zenodo concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19074199 as a separate 'Software archive (all versions)' line. Do not name a version number. Both DOIs were verified: the arXiv page, and the Zenodo API for the concept DOI, creators and 'describes arXiv:2603.10704'.
3. Render the block as an h2 id="cite" section on the home page via a new function in pages_site.py (stays under 30 lines; the file is 101 lines). Escape all values with text.esc.
4. Make the footer 'Cite LabConstrictor' link point to the home page plus anchor (e.g. `{{ 'index.html#cite' | url }}`), not a bare '#cite'. check_site.py then verifies the anchor.
5. Close the drift risk with a build-time check, not a second copy: build_site already has --template-dir, so fail the build, naming the file, if the template README lacks the arXiv DOI string. Add a test for the page containing the DOI and a failure test for a missing key or a README without the DOI.
Wording: 'If you use LabConstrictor, please cite: <authors>. <title>. arXiv preprint 2026. <doi link>'. This is the README's wording and needs no new claims. Add the line 'Software archive: Zenodo' with the concept DOI. Do not add 'recommended' unless the authors say so.
Authors to decide: concept DOI or version DOI, and the exact name forms. Zenodo and DataCite print 'Hidalgo Cenalmor, Iván' and 'Rivera Pineda, Marcela Xiomara', while arXiv and the README print 'Iván Hidalgo-Cenalmor' and 'Marcela Xiomara Rivera Pineda'. Use the arXiv/README form for the paper line.
verdicts.evidence: Footer overrides/main.html:100 links https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20758747 with the text 'Cite LabConstrictor'. grep shows `citation_doi` is used by no script. Built site/index.html has only the footer 'Cite LabConstrictor' text. Template README lines 66-69: the Citation section gives the five authors, the title and arXiv DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2603.10704. WebFetch of arxiv.org/abs/2603.10704 confirms the authors, title and DOI, submitted 11 Mar 2026, no journal ref. Zenodo API: record 20758747 is version 0.0.2 dated 2026-06-19, conceptdoi 10.5281/zenodo.19074199, five creators. The template repo has no tags.

verdicts.misleading_risk: Step 2 (resolving Crossref/DataCite metadata and formatting references) adds a network dependency, third-party text and reference styling that must be exactly right. It is disproportionate for 6 apps, so drop it. The sentence 'No publication is listed' shown on 4 of 6 pages can be read as 'no paper exists'. It must say what is true: the app's listing gives none. Pointing app visitors to the LabConstrictor citation for 'the packaging' asserts that the app's authors want that, which is unverified. 'Version used: vX' repeats the release line already on the page.
verdicts.refined_proposal:
Do step 1 only, trimmed.
(a) In pages_apps.py, replace the Details 'Cite' row with a short section `cite_section(app)` after `using_section`. It is a h2 id="cite" with 'If you use this app in your work, please cite:' and the existing doi link (escaped). Remove the row from details_list so the DOI is written once. Keep `doi` optional in the schema.
(b) When there is no doi, show one factual line: 'This app's listing names no publication to cite.' Do not add a recommendation or the LabConstrictor link. The author decides whether to show this line at all; if not, show nothing, which is allowed for optional fields.
(c) Change the schema description of `doi` to 'DOI of the paper to cite' (an archive DOI is not the paper). NucleiSky and CellTracksColab already use the paper DOI. NucleiSky's README also has a Zenodo software DOI, 10.5281/zenodo.21071484, which is not in its manifest.
(d) Add tests for the present and absent cases.
(e) Separately and optionally, the VLab4Mic owners may add `doi: 10.64898/2026.06.02.729521` to labconstrictor-app.yaml. The DOI is verified: Crossref gives the title 'VLab4Mic: prediction of structural resolvability in super-resolution microscopy' on bioRxiv, and the README's BibTeX gives the same DOI. Owners confirm it is the preferred citation. This is a change in another repo, which this audit does not make.
No snapshot change, no Crossref fetch.
verdicts.evidence: pages_apps.py:152-153 renders the 'Cite' row inside details_list, which page_app calls last. Built pages: only celltrackscolab (10.1371/journal.pbio.3002740) and nucleisky (10.1242/jcs.265152) have 'Cite'. build/snapshot.json: doi is present only for those two of 6 apps. VLab4Mic's manifest has no doi although its README (lines 58-72) gives the bioRxiv DOI 10.64898/2026.06.02.729521. The schema line 36 reads 'DOI of the paper or archive to cite.'

verdicts.misleading_risk: Moderate. 'Developed by <five names>' is an unsupported claim. arXiv supports 'authors of the preprint', not 'developed' or contribution roles. 'Affiliations, contributions and funding are in the preprint' could not be verified: the PDF text could not be read via fetch, so affiliations, funding and the contributions section are unverifiable here. Do not name the Cell Migration Lab as an affiliation without a primary source. Repeating the author list in a separate paragraph duplicates G1.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Merge into G1; no separate section. The G1 citation block already names the preprint authors, which is the credit. Add nothing about funders or affiliations until an author supplies approved text. Footer: keep 'A project of the Cell Migration Lab' and the link to #cite from G1, retitled 'Cite LabConstrictor'. Delete the unused `copyright: © Cell Migration Lab` from mkdocs.yml (the overrides footer never renders it; 0 matches for '©' in the built pages), or leave it alone. Do not add 'Developed by' wording or role labels. A funding or acknowledgement paragraph needs authors' approved wording, copied from the preprint by an author.
verdicts.evidence: Footer text 'A project of the Cell Migration Lab' (main.html:102) is the only credit. site/index.html and an app page contain no '©'. The arXiv listing gives the five authors but no affiliations. The PDF fetch could not read the body, so the funding and affiliation claims are unverifiable.

verdicts.misleading_risk: High if done from the site side. Paper authors are not necessarily the software authors, so copying a paper's author list into an app manifest would credit people unverified. Do not infer authors from the GitHub org or the repo owner. The footer sentence 'Apps are made and maintained by their own authors' is unverified for the 6 current apps: all six registry entries are repos in the CellMigrationLab org, and the VLab4Mic clone's origin is HenriquesLab/LabConstrictor-VLab4Mic. Someone must confirm who maintains each app.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Site code: no change; the 'Authors' row already renders and is escaped. Ask each app's owners to add `authors:` (name, optional orcid, matching the schema) to labconstrictor-app.yaml. Add no names on their behalf; absent evidence the author is 'unknown'. For VLab4Mic, the README's BibTeX lists 8 paper authors (Crossref confirms), but that is the paper, not necessarily the app, so the owners decide. Leave the footer as is, or use author-approved text such as 'Each app page names its authors when the app's listing gives them', which is true by construction. Tell owners the facts and let them act in their own repos. No site edit now.
verdicts.evidence: build/snapshot.json: no app manifest has an `authors` key (0 of 6), and the built app pages have no 'Authors' dt. pages_apps.py:147-148 renders the row when authors exist. The schema author def has `name` (required) and an optional ORCID. Registry entries show owner CellMigrationLab for all six repos. VLab4Mic README names the main project at HenriquesLab/VLab4Mic. Crossref author families are Martínez, Saraiva, Shakespeare, Bates, Owen, Leterrier, Del Rosario, Henriques.
